After Boomerang Basics resolves and goes to the graveyard, there would be 5 Lessons in the graveyard, making Combustion Technique deal 7 damage. However, the sequencing matters: casting Boomerang Basics first (which is a Lesson) puts it in the graveyard, powering up Combustion Technique for later. But bouncing Ouroboroid means the opponent can just replay it. Combustion Technique would permanently remove it (exile it, even). The better line might have been to cast Combustion Technique targeting Ouroboroid directly - with 4 Lessons in graveyard (Willowrush Verge x2 aren't Lessons, but Stormchaser's Talent isn't a Lesson either - let me recheck the graveyard: Willowrush Verge, Willowrush Verge, Stormchaser's Talent, Abandon Attachments). Only Abandon Attachments is a Lesson in the graveyard, so Combustion Technique would deal 2+1=3 damage. Ouroboroid is 1/3 base but at beginning of combat gets +1/+1 counters equal to its power, so it could be bigger. Actually wait - it's currently on the battlefield as listed without any notation of counters, so it might be a 1/3 still (or could have gotten counters from previous combat). If it's a 1/3, 3 damage kills it. But if Boomerang Basics is cast first (it's a Lesson), then Combustion Technique deals 2+2=4. Either way, bouncing is only temporary removal while Combustion Technique would exile it permanently. Using Boomerang Basics here wastes the permanent removal opportunity since the opponent will just replay Ouroboroid next turn.
